label: July 27–August 02
title: “I Am Doing a Great Work” —  Ezra 1; 3–7; Nehemiah 2; 4

items.text: Though the Jewish people had been captives for seventy years, losing their land and temple, God had not forgotten them. He declared through Jeremiah, 'I will visit you, and perform my good word toward you, in causing you to return.' The Lord made a way for His people to return to Jerusalem and, more importantly, to their covenants.

God raised up servants like Zerubbabel, Ezra, and Nehemiah to accomplish 'a great work.' Zerubbabel oversaw the rebuilding of the house of the Lord, Ezra helped the people turn their hearts back to God’s law, and Nehemiah led the rebuilding of Jerusalem's walls. Their experiences inform and inspire us, for we too are doing a great work.

The Lord inspires people to accomplish His purposes. He inspired King Cyrus to send Jews back to Jerusalem to rebuild the temple. Observe how the Lord works through individuals, even those not members of His Church, to further His divine plan and build His kingdom on earth.

When the Jews were allowed to return and rebuild the temple decades after its destruction, they experienced profound joy. This celebration reminds us of the sacredness of the house of the Lord and prompts us to ponder our own feelings about temples and the blessings they bring to our lives.

The Lord’s work is often met with opposition, just as it was for Zerubbabel and Nehemiah. By understanding the challenges they faced and how they responded, we can learn to persevere in God’s work, even when we encounter difficulties. God has an important work for each of us to do.

Zerubbabel and his companions faced significant opposition while rebuilding the temple, yet they responded by continuing their sacred labor with faith. This teaches us that despite challenges, we should press forward with determination, relying on God’s strength and guidance to complete His work.

Nehemiah and his people demonstrated a remarkable 'mind to work' in rebuilding Jerusalem's walls. This dedication, coupled with the 'good hand of God' upon them, allowed them to overcome formidable obstacles. We too can experience divine assistance as we serve the Savior with all our hearts.

Ezra, a priest and scribe, diligently taught the people God's law, helping them to understand and repent. His efforts led to a spiritual revival, demonstrating the power of scripture and the importance of returning to the Lord's covenants. His dedication reminds us to cherish and teach divine truth.

The rebuilding of the temple and Jerusalem's walls were acts of faith and obedience. These experiences underscore the importance of the house of the Lord and the spiritual protection found in keeping sacred covenants. We are all engaged in a great work that involves His house and His law.

The Lord’s promise to guide and strengthen His people is evident in the stories of Ezra and Nehemiah. As we face our own challenges and strive to do His work, we can trust that His hand will be upon us, empowering us to accomplish His divine purposes.
